doc.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15

chapter: Joe Rene: Lewis, the Rena band and New Orleans
title: Rene's birth record, his father, and Buddy Petit's wah-wah mute
summary: Rene checks his baptismal record, remembers his guitarist father, and credits Buddy Petit's derby with leading him to invent the wah-wah.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: So I went down to the Catholic Church. I was born to the Catholic Church. I went down there, and I got my boy's sister, and I was surprised. And I always owned the impression that I was born with Marshall Levin, or the first. But when I look on that verse, it was Marshall Levin. Marshall Levin. Mm. Marshall Levin, 1897. My dad was a musician too. Oh, was he? Yeah. He used to play guitar, bandolin, bass. What was his name? Henry, Renny. He was working for a lot of war lines when they was on Burgundy Street. That's up I remember. That's your, I was a child then. And I understand, from what I can understand from old him, he's the first fella that thought to puttin' that twirl in the guitar. I mean? But when he wanted to play guitar, it's a different position. He didn't know how to make it. I couldn't remember, so he put it down in the market with some buttons off his shirt. That's, that's facts. I was surprised when a fella told that. Yeah. Do you remember Buddy Petit? Oh yeah, sure. I played with Buddy Petit. What did you think of him, Mr. Trumpet, right? Boy, he, he had a nice start. He's the first one to start with them derbies, you know, put them derbies on there. And, the way it is at that time, trumpet players ain't that way now, I don't agree. But, the other trumpet always tried to do one another. See? So, when I seen him at the derby, derby, derby, derby, I went out to the fresh market and got a coconut. Cut it in half. And, they ain't no brother do this, I don't want to trumpet, wah-wah. That's where they, that wah-wah started.
Wah-wah, we started from there. Mm-hmm. Yeah. That's right. I'll never forget that.
